commits.message:
Record the pooled DA committee bond decision and its vocabulary (#685)

Every attestation locks its own DA bond today, and an honest block's bond has no release path. The owner replaced it with one DA bond pool for the whole committee: anyone may top it up, an attestation applies only while the pool holds one DA bond of backing, a lost availability challenge slashes the pool, and only the governance quorum can withdraw, after a delay. The decision record keeps the rejected options (a time-based per-block reclaim, and one bond per committee member) with the reasons they lost. CONTEXT.md gains the data-availability bonding terms, so the implementation tickets #686-#693 share one vocabulary.

Add the node L1 rollback redesign plan and its code audits

Revision 4 of the proposed rollback redesign: owner rulings D1-D3, the P0 verifications, and the ticket breakdown in section 11. The six audits it cites (deletion, retained MPF roots, mempool reinjection, projection acceptance, recovery callers, schema draft) sit beside it so the plan's claims can be checked. Nothing in it is implemented yet, and its tickets are not published.

Require public profiles to wait out a fork deeper than finality

An event's inclusion time is its transaction's validity upper bound
plus the event wait, and a header's end time is its commit's validity
upper bound, at most the maximum validity range after the commit's
lower bound. Every event a header must include was therefore on L1 at
least (event wait - maximum validity range) before the commit became
valid.

deployment:check now requires every public profile to size that span
as its confirmation depth in blocks, using the same 20 s mean block
interval and safety factor of two as the DA response budget:
event_wait_ms >= max_validity_range_ms + confirmation_depth * 40 s.
An honest block can then omit a required event only if L1 rolls back
past its finality depth or produces under half its mean block rate for
the whole span, so the margin is probabilistic. Mainnet and
preprod-public satisfy it (floor 1,680,000 ms). The README records
that under the stricter 3N/f worst case it uses to size the event
wait, preprod-public's 30 minutes leave 22 blocks after the validity
range, not 30.

The testing profiles are exempt and accept the short-fork omission
risk that their 5 min event wait leaves. The block-interval constants
lose their DA-specific names now that two budgets share them.

Check the native owner before the phase-4 bootstrap touches the devnet

Only write-acceptance-env.sh checked the owner binary, and bootstrap ran it after the whole protocol bootstrap, so a missing or mismatched binary was found only after the L1 work, and rerunning bootstrap would repeat it on an initialized chain. The resolve-and-refuse logic now lives in native-owner.mjs; bootstrap runs it first through native-owner-preflight.sh, before compose up, and write-acceptance-env.sh pins its result. The README says to rerun only write-acceptance-env.sh after a late refusal.

Leave the retention sweep interval to its derived default in .env.example

The template set WAIT_BETWEEN_RETENTION_SWEEPS=60000 while its own comment and the READMEs document the derived default min(900000, DA attestation timeout / 4). Any operator copying the template silently overrode that default. The line is now commented out, like L1_VIEW_FATAL_MS.

Pin the native MPF owner in the live acceptance env checklist

The node refuses to listen without MPF_NATIVE_OWNER_BINARY_SHA256, which .env.example leaves blank, so following the checklist led to a crash loop. The checklist now names the owner path, sidecar and the command that prints the image's pin, and says to re-pin after each rebuild.

Require an explicit committee finality depth

The committee launch defaulted CARDANO_FINALITY_DEPTH to 2 while preprod-testing pins confirmation depth 3, and the committee refuses a runtime/manifest mismatch. The launch now requires the value to be set to the manifest's l1Finality.confirmationDepth.

State the deposit validity upper bound as 120 s

History submissions are valid from 60 s in the past for 180 s, so the upper bound is at most 120 s out, not 60 s.

Set a deadline for public DA retrieval of each header

The committee prunes a merged non-head block's payload at end_time plus 1.5 x maturity (1,350 s on preprod-testing). Live acceptance now says to retrieve each header's payload as soon as it is attested and before that horizon, and that a later not-found is expected pruning.

Derive the automatic-merge wait from block maturity

The await-automatic-merge step waited 900 s, shorter than the earliest merge of a header committed with a future end time under 900 s maturity. The budget is now maturity + 420 s end-time lead + 20 s alignment + 180 s confirmation + 300 s for sequential merges (1,820 s on preprod-testing), read from the compiled profile, and the runner timeout is 60 s longer than the loop's deadline.

Mark the walkthrough's manual commit and merge calls devnet-only

The deposit/send/withdraw walkthrough called the admin /commit and /merge endpoints by hand, which bypasses the commit and automatic merge fibers that fresh-deploy acceptance must prove. It now says those calls are for a local devnet only, and live acceptance points at its withdrawal and payout commands with the instruction to wait for the fibers instead.

Require the negligence timeout to cover the block-commitment gap

The scheduler's neglected-event guard accepts an event whose inclusion
time equals the tail block's end time, which that block already
includes. That is harmless only while inclusion + negligence timeout
can never precede tail end + maximum inactivity, and the operator
watchdog assumes the same ordering. Profile validation now enforces it
instead of relying on the shipped values.

Never count a suspended history authority row as a live owner

Release and suspend stamp lease_until with clock_timestamp(). This
machine's wall clock steps backwards by about a second every half
minute, so a released row could read as live again before the next
generation's acquire, and acquire refused the successor with "History
authority still has a live owner". A suspended row confers no
authority, so acquire now ignores its lease end. The restart helper
uses the same rule and says whether the refusing lease belongs to the
stopped owner or to another one.

Name the live history lease a restarted test owner loses to

A full node run once failed the endpoint-independence restart with only
"History authority still has a live owner", after the restart's own
release check had passed. The helper now reports the authority row it
lost to, the stopped owner's token and the worker database, so the next
occurrence identifies the holder.

Clear the history authority before the local mutation job tests

The fixture producer gate refuses any acquired history owner row, and an
earlier file on the same worker shard can leave one behind, which turned
all seven fixture-producing tests red when the file ran after such a file.
